# Modern Approaches for Fraud Detection in Highly Imbalanced Transaction Datasets

## Summary

The most effective evaluation metrics for fraud detection in highly imbalanced datasets are a combined F1 score and g-mean, in that specific order. [S5] Traditional accuracy metrics are inadequate for evaluating fraud detection models due to the extreme imbalance in fraudulent transactions. [S5] F1 score and g-mean are recommended as effective performance measures for unbalanced datasets. [S5] ROC curve (AuROC) and Average Precision are commonly used performance measures in credit card fraud detection. [S5] Credit card fraud detection datasets typically have over 99% legitimate transactions. [S2] SMOTE oversampling with a 200% ratio can significantly improve dataset balance in fraud detection. [S1]

## Key findings

- The most effective evaluation metrics for fraud detection in highly imbalanced datasets are a combined F1 score and g-mean, in that specific order. [S5]
- Traditional accuracy metrics are inadequate for evaluating fraud detection models due to the extreme imbalance in fraudulent transactions. [S5]
- F1 score and g-mean are recommended as effective performance measures for unbalanced datasets. [S5]
- ROC curve (AuROC) and Average Precision are commonly used performance measures in credit card fraud detection. [S5]
- SMOTE oversampling with a 200% ratio can significantly improve dataset balance in fraud detection. [S1]

## Evaluation Metrics

The most effective evaluation metrics for fraud detection in highly imbalanced datasets are a combined F1 score and g-mean, in that specific order. [S5]

F1 score and g-mean are recommended as effective performance measures for unbalanced datasets. [S5]

Traditional accuracy metrics are inadequate for evaluating fraud detection models due to the extreme imbalance in fraudulent transactions. [S5]

ROC curve (AuROC) and Average Precision are commonly used performance measures in credit card fraud detection. [S5]

## Data Imbalance Characteristics

Credit card fraud detection datasets typically have over 99% legitimate transactions. [S2]

## Data Preprocessing Techniques

SMOTE oversampling with a 200% ratio can significantly improve dataset balance in fraud detection. [S1]

SMOTE proves valuable in scenarios with extreme imbalances, such as health insurance fraud detection where fraudulent claims can be as rare as 1:99. [S1]

- The evidence does not provide specific details on the performance of other oversampling techniques beyond SMOTE.
